These quantities reduce to Gaussian covariance optimizations, and the capacity is attained by pure Gaussian signals with Gaussian displacement modulation, independently across channel uses. The proof combines geodesic convexity of entanglement for pure Gaussian states with a relative-entropy inequality for arbitrary states. We also obtain a closed formula for the entanglement cost of a family of four-mode bound entangled states.

papers.title: FastSpecFit: Spectrophotometric Modeling of 38 Million Extragalactic Targets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Second Data Release
papers.summary: Optical spectrophotometry provides a direct window into the physical conditions, kinematics, and formation histories of galaxies and quasars. FastSpecFit is an open-source Python software package that forward-models each Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectrum jointly with its broadband photometry, convolving stellar-population synthesis and emission-line templates with each fiber's native spectral resolution. This forward-modeling approach preserves DESI's uncorrelated pixel statistics, fits a typical spectrum in ~0.1 s of single-core time, and scales to tens of millions of objects, with uncertainties estimated via Monte Carlo resampling. FastSpecFit measures stellar velocity dispersions, non-parametric star-formation histories, stellar masses, star-formation rates, dust attenuation, K-corrections, rest-frame magnitudes, and fluxes and equivalent widths for 46 emission lines, including separate narrow and broad components for the Balmer lines. We describe these algorithms in detail, validate the measurements against independent codes, and present the resulting value-added catalog for DESI Data Release 2, which provides spectrophotometric and physical properties for 38 million extragalactic targets at 0<z<4. We also release a companion photometry-only catalog and document the catalogs previously released for the DESI Early Data Release and Data Release 1.
papers.comment: Submitted to AJ; 73 pages, 13 figures, 7 tables

papers.title: A novel method for dust evolution in protoplanetary disks and a new criterion for gap opening
papers.summary: We present the Grain Residence-Time Method (GRTM), a computationally efficient particle-tracking approach for studying dust evolution and trapping in protoplanetary disks. By reconstructing steady-state dust distributions from particle residence times, this method provides a way to obtain radial dust surface density profiles without directly evolving the dust as a fluid. We compare the GRTM with dust profiles computed via standard methods using the $\texttt{FARGO3D}$ code, which models the dust as a pressureless fluid, and find very good agreement over a wide range of parameter space. Finally, we investigate how dust gap formation depends on the planet-to-star mass ratio ($q$) and Stokes number ($\mathrm{St}$), through a parameter study, establishing an empirical criterion for dust gap opening. In doing so, we have discovered a new regime of gap opening for small grains with $St \lesssim 10^{-2}$ and for planet mass well below Jupiter's, which is likely very relevant for gaps seen in ALMA images.

papers.title: Can Verifiable PIR Match the Online Efficiency of SimplePIR?
papers.summary: Verifiable Private Information Retrieval (vPIR) ensures that a malicious server cannot return tampered database records, but it traditionally incurs significant overhead compared to classical PIR.Recent advancements, notably VeriSimplePIR, approach the online efficiency of SimplePIR by introducing a proof preprocessing phase and requiring only lightweight client-side online verification. However, this scheme relies on an additional Short Integer Solution (SIS) assumption and SIS-based commitments, which only support relaxed range proofs. Consequently, these schemes are forced to adopt significantly weaker parameter choices, resulting in additional online overhead. In this paper, we propose a novel vPIR protocol that employs a newly designed error-correcting code-based commitment scheme as the database digest. This approach (i)supports efficient proofs of linear relations, (ii) achieves precise range proofs and (iii) eliminates the reliance on the SIS assumption. Thus, our scheme successfully adopts parameter choices identical to those of SimplePIR. As a result, our vPIR protocol is the first to achieve exactly the same online communication and server computation costs as SimplePIR, while keeping online client computation nearly identical. Additionally, compared to VeriSimplePIR,our protocol reduces online communication and client-side computation by approximately 20%, and decreases online server-side computation by over 35%.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication at the 2027 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (IEEE S&P 2027)

papers.title: Arboreus: A Realistic Boreal Forest Simulator with Topographic Terrain and Satellite-Informed Parametric Tree Distributions
papers.summary: This work presents Arboreus, a realistic Boreal forest simulator, developed to support statistical validation of robotic autonomy algorithms in Boreal forest environments. Arboreus presents an automated methodology for synthesizing large-scale, data-informed, plausible forest worlds from parametric trees, height-variant terrain, and satellite-informed tree density distributions. The parametric generation of dominant Boreal tree species such as Birch, Spruce, and Pine is guided by trunk, canopy, and foliage parameters, extracted from growth studies in the Nordic areas. Tree distribution in an area of interest is guided by the Copernicus satellite dataset, which provides tree cover density and dominant species type at up to 10m raster resolution. The forest floor generation is guided by topographic data from the Swedish cadastral agency to produce realistic data-informed terrains. Given coordinates and extents of forested areas of interest, Arboreus synthesizes data-informed plausible forests, while offering flexibility to inject user observations of real forests (detail, age, dimensionality and tree count), which is critical for realistic synthetic data generation and for the testing of feature-sensitive autonomy algorithms. The applicability of Arboreus for benchmarking and validation of robot autonomy for different robot mobilities is demonstrated in Gazebosim, Unreal Engine, and Isaac Sim physics engines. The applicability of Arboreus as a source of synthetic forest data and its potential to support downstream forest resource mapping research (volume estimation, tree instance segmentation and stem attribute estimation) is also demonstrated. Arboreus has been open-sourced along with a dataset comprising 25 Boreal forest worlds of size 1000m2 corresponding to three real forest sites.

papers.title: Optimising Recruitment and Sample Allocation in Multi-Site Rare Disease Studies
papers.summary: Clinical research in rare diseases is challenged by the limited availability and broad geographical distribution of eligible patients. This necessitates multi-centre collaboration and strategic selection of analytical laboratories based on capacity, cost, and capability. We present a mathematical framework based on cardinality optimisation to support key operational decisions in study design, balancing clinical relevance, feasibility, budgetary constraints, and logistical factors. The framework was implemented in the Reconstruction and Computational Modelling for Inherited Metabolic Diseases (Recon4IMD) project, aiming to recruit 1,900 diagnosed patients across 24 healthcare centres and eight metabolomic laboratories. Compared to both proportional heuristic and greedy marginal allocation baselines, the proposed optimisation model consistently achieved higher recruitment yields in simulated multi-centre scenarios and reduced metabolomic analysis costs by approximately 30% under unconstrained conditions. Notably, both the heuristic and greedy allocation baselines became infeasible under progressively tighter laboratory capacity constraints, whereas the optimised model maintained feasibility and cost control. These findings highlight the value of integrated optimisation strategies for improving recruitment, platform selection, and sample allocation in complex, resource-limited research settings.

papers.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
papers.summary: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated. Here, we develop a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite function-based (Hermite-B) DVR that adapts naturally to magnetic confinement, efficiently representing compressed wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths while remaining centered in regions relevant to the scalar confinement potential. This ensures accurate treatment of the field-dependent kinetic energy while addressing two key challenges: maintaining accuracy from the Zeeman to Landau regimes and accommodating diverse confinement potentials. We also introduce a spatial restriction scheme that confines Hermite DVR grid points to a fixed-length domain, enabling compact representations for smooth potentials. The method is benchmarked for two-dimensional quantum dots in perpendicular magnetic fields against analytical models and compared with finite-grid, sine DVR, and field-free Hermite DVR calculations. The performance of field-independent DVR methods for magnetically confined systems is also investigated for the first time. Excellent agreement with exact analytical spectra and wavefunctions is obtained, with Hermite-B requiring the fewest basis functions and smaller Hamiltonian matrices, improving computational efficiency. Applications to arbitrary confinement potentials and tilted magnetic fields demonstrate its versatility beyond analytically solvable systems. The proposed method offers a robust, accurate, and efficient framework for large-scale calculations of realistic semiconductor nanostructures and molecular systems in external magnetic fields.

papers.title: Who Pays for Byzantine Robustness? Validity, Data-Share Dictatorships, and Fairness When Only a Few Hospitals Collaborate
papers.summary: Clinical federated learning (FL) collaborations typically connect only three to six hospitals, yet Byzantine-robust aggregation rules are designed and benchmarked on synthetic partitions across dozens of equal-sized clients. We conduct an empirical audit of eight standard aggregation rules: FedAvg, coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, Krum, Multi-Krum, Bulyan, geometric median (GeoMed), and Centered Clipping (CC). We evaluate both unweighted and sample-size-weighted variants across three cross-silo medical datasets from the FLamby benchmark: Fed-Heart-Disease ($n = 4$ hospitals), Fed-TCGA-BRCA ($n = 6$ regions), and Fed-ISIC2019 ($n = 6$ centres). We execute 54,214 training runs across enumerated attacker coalitions ($f \in \{1, 2\}$) paired with exact-twin leave-out controls that decompose performance drops into honest data loss versus adversarial attack damage. We report three findings. First, client-count validity checks fail to capture breakdown in skewed medical consortia: while $n = 6, f = 1$ satisfies every count condition except Bulyan's, assigning sample-size weights turns median and GeoMed into a clean-model dictatorship whenever a single hospital holds more than half the training data, and causes weighted median, GeoMed, and CC to collapse when that dominant centre attacks. Second, exact-twin leave-out controls reveal that when the largest hospital attacks, the apparent failure of count-based robust rules is predominantly caused by the loss of honest training data (7.5 to 10.4 points on ISIC) rather than adversarial perturbation (2.3 to 3.8 points on ISIC). Conversely, weight-dependent rules suffer large true attack damage (16.1 to 25.1 points on ISIC). Third, unweighted robust rules consistently discount whichever institution generates the most atypical parameter updates, penalizing the smallest hospital on Heart but penalizing larger institutions on TCGA and ISIC.

papers.title: A free-energy approach for stochastic reaction-drift-diffusion lattice simulations of crowded biological systems
papers.summary: Molecular size alters spatial distributions, reaction equilibria, and transport in crowded mixtures, but resolving individual particle encounters can make large stochastic simulations computationally costly. We developed a lattice-based framework for simulating reaction-drift-diffusion systems with volume exclusion captured as a free energy functional in each voxel. Changes in this free energy, together with external one-body potentials, modify diffusion and reaction propensities. Our framework accommodates mixtures of particle sizes without resolving each particle's position within a voxel. We implemented our framework in an operator splitting scheme and compared our predictions with off-lattice interacting-particle simulations. Inclusion of the local free energy functional improved spatial occupancies and shifts in reaction equilibria relative to point-particle simulations. With separate approximations for larger spheres and polymers, we simulated crowding-induced slowing and spatial segregation. We then modeled motor proteins' traffic jams on a structured track representing a microtubule. Our results demonstrate how local composition can inform stochastic reaction and transport rates without resolving individual encounters.

papers.title: Tunable Microresonator Arrays Induced by Geometric Phase
papers.summary: Unlike periodic field-intensity patterns, which can be generated by interference of coherent beams, periodic material structures are usually created by periodic modification. In contrast, we show here that a millimeter-long bundle of four conventional side-coupled optical fibers with a slowly varying transverse arrangement can support a nearly periodic array of whispering-gallery-mode microresonators, whose period can be tuned mechanically down to about $100\,μ\mathrm{m}$.

papers.title: Exact classical bounds of bipartite correlation Bell inequalities using improved branch-and-bound
papers.summary: We present an improved branch-and-bound (IBB) algorithm for the exact computation of classical (local) bounds of bipartite correlation Bell inequalities. We strengthen pruning in the standard BB algorithm in two ways: a heuristic search based on see-saw iteration supplies a strong initial lower bound, and greedy row reordering of the Bell matrix reduces the tail bounds used during the exact search. An OpenMP implementation combines these improvements with shared-memory parallelism and dynamic work redistribution. Random-matrix benchmarks show substantial runtime reductions in matrix sizes, while explicit constructions demonstrate exact local-bound computations for square matrices up to $130 \times 130$ and rectangular matrices of sizes up to $81 \times 321$. Applications provide improved lower bounds on finite-order Grothendieck constants for $d=3,4,5,7$ and uniform-input XOR games with quantum-to-classical ratios exceeding $\sqrt2$. The method retains an exponential worst-case search for this NP-hard optimization problem, and its practical performance depends on matrix structure and tail-bound preprocessing depth.

papers.title: Weighted Proportional Toll Sharing on General Highway Networks
papers.summary: We extend the Segments Equal Sharing (SES) method of \citet{wu2024} from line highways to general highway networks, including networks with cycles. The input is an exogenously specified profile of route flows. We introduce the Weighted Proportional Sharing (WPS) method, which distributes each route's mileage revenue in proportion to weighted segment lengths and its fixed-surcharge revenue in proportion to positive segment surcharges. Route SES is recovered under homogeneous weights within each revenue component. We show that WPS is the sum of two weighted Shapley allocations and that the underlying route games extend the dividend and Shapley representation of linear SES. Two axiomatic characterizations identify WPS. The first uses additivity and proportional treatment of segments used on every positive-revenue route. The second combines sub-highway efficiency and weighted average balanced contributions under a route cancellation rule. We also extend Segments Proportional Sharing to general networks, identify it with the $τ$ value of the corresponding route game, and characterize it axiomatically. For Segments Compensated Sharing we characterize a weighted average tree allocation by consistency across rooted branch settlements and averaging under a specified root lottery. A cyclic example shows that different route splits can change the allocation even when origin--destination volumes and aggregate toll revenue are held fixed.

papers.title: Impact of errors-on-errors on the PDF determination from combined HERA data
papers.summary: We study how the determination of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data is affected when the quoted sizes of the systematic errors are themselves treated as uncertain. We refer to these uncertainties informally as errors-on-errors and account for them using the Gamma Variance Model, which treats the squared quoted systematic errors as Gamma-distributed estimates of unknown variances. As a result, the usual quadratic nuisance parameter constraints in the $χ^2$ are replaced with logarithmic ones. We present two applications of the framework. In the first, a robustness test estimates the largest errors-on-errors effects that could be present in our reproduction of the HERAPDF2.0 NNLO fit, reducing $χ^2/n_{\rm dof}$ from 1363/1131 to 1306/1131, with the main impact concentrated at low Bjorken $x$ and low squared momentum transfer, $Q^2$. Comparable reductions are observed with a more flexible small-$x$ parametrisation, both at fixed NNLO and with NNLO+NLL$_x$ resummation. In the second, the error-on-error parameters are instead assigned a priori, as they would be in a PDF determination intended for publication. Taken together, the results indicate that errors-on-errors can account for a substantial part of the apparent data-theory tension in the combined HERA dataset, improving the inferred compatibility and widening the fitted PDF uncertainties without appreciably displacing the PDFs or cross-section predictions themselves.

papers.title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
papers.summary: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_χ=1$ TeV, $δ=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $τ^+τ^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.

papers.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
papers.summary: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. Sequential test-time scaling can improve exploitation performance, but larger budgets do not ensure sustained exploration: agents often stop with budget remaining. Yet what happens when execution continues beyond stopping remains underexplored. We investigate this gap on ExploitBench using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. We find additional verified gains after the first stop response, but gains diminish over longer execution. We identify two patterns associated with less productive continuation: an increasing proportion of stop responses within the same context and earlier stopping associated with summaries retaining impossibility judgments about unachieved capabilities. To test whether context management can elicit further capability, we propose SCoRe, which compacts context at stop bursts and marks these judgments as unproven. SCoRe improves verified capability over summary-based continuation and other evaluated context-management baselines. With SCoRe, MiMo reaches a capability coverage score of 67.0% at 2,000 turns, exceeding both 32.4% under the original stopping policy and the 58.6% computed for GPT-5.5 from ExploitBench's 300-turn reference results on the same tasks. These findings show that stopping need not mark an agent's exploitation limit, and that continued execution with context management can elicit substantial further capability.

papers.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- The evolution of the radio-loud AGN fraction-stellar mass relation to $z\sim3$ in the Euclid Deep Field North
papers.summary: The incidence of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (RLAGN) and their energetic output via AGN feedback are crucial in understanding the evolution of galaxies and the large-scale structure of the Universe. In the local Universe, the incidence of RLAGN has been shown to correlate strongly with host galaxy properties, particularly stellar mass. Using the large-area survey capabilities provided by Euclid and the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR), we present the first study of the RLAGN incidence--stellar mass relation to $z=3.0$. We perform a stringent analysis accounting for cross-matching reliability and stellar-mass incompleteness. In addition, we test the robustness of our results against AGN and host galaxy classification. This yields a sample of $3\,154$ RLAGN in the Euclid Deep Field North, comprising $2\,803$ low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs). We find that the LERG incidence as a function of stellar mass and radio luminosity follows a tight correlation over more than two orders of magnitude in stellar mass to $z=3.0$. The slope of the power-law relation decreases from $γ\approx2.5$ in the local Universe to $γ\approx1.0$ at $z=3.0$, indicating a relative increase in low-mass LERGs at earlier epochs. Separating the LERG population into actively star-forming and quiescent galaxies reveals that quiescent LERGs show a much steeper relation between incidence and stellar mass, with $γ\approx2.5$ compared to star-forming LERGs that show $γ\approx1.5$. However, the relation seems to be independent of whether galaxies are star-forming or quiescent at $z\geq2$, where both populations show relatively flat relations with $γ\approx1.0$. Our results suggest an evolutionary picture in which the LERG population transitions from cold-mode, merger-dominated accretion at earlier epochs to a scenario in which systems require a massive hot halo to fuel the AGN in the local Universe.

papers.title: Sequential Conditional Paired-Sample Testing with Applications to Online Monitoring
papers.summary: We study sequential conditional paired-sample testing, where observations arrive over time and the goal is to continuously assess whether two conditional distributions are equal given a common set of covariates. This problem arises naturally in model monitoring, where distributional changes must be detected without a prespecified terminal sample size, and in online comparisons, where responses are compared conditional on subject-level characteristics. We propose SCPT, an anytime-valid testing procedure for conditional distributions based on sequentially constructed conditional kernel discrepancy statistics and test martingales. The proposed method is nonparametric and accommodates a broad class of data-generating processes beyond the i.i.d. setting. We establish time-uniform Type I error control and derive asymptotic power guarantees under suitable regularity conditions. We also develop several useful extensions to address different needs, including testing under broader dependence structures, comparisons involving multiple auxiliary streams, and conditional goodness-of-fit testing. Simulations and real-data experiments show that SCPT effectively detects conditional distributional differences in streaming data, demonstrating its practical utility in a wide range of real-world applications.

papers.title: The Whole Warps the Parts: Attentional Certainty Modulates Ensemble-Induced Bias in Visualizations
papers.summary: Data visualizations often require viewers to extract both ensemble statistics and individual values from collections of graphical marks. Yet individual items embedded within an ensemble can be systematically biased by that context. Prior studies have reported both repulsion away from and attraction toward ensemble statistics, but these effects have been observed across different conditions. We test whether task or attentional certainty explains these opposing forms of ensemble-induced bias. In Study 1, observers briefly viewed ensembles of differently sized circles and then judged the size of an individual circle embedded within the ensemble. Using a common stimulus generation framework, we tested both identification and discrimination when the target was specified before or after the ensemble, and an additional no-cue identification condition without a specified target. Under the shared cued conditions, effects were predominantly repulsive or near zero in both identification and discrimination. In contrast, eliminating target-specific information reversed ensemble-induced bias from repulsion to attraction. Identification precision also decreased systematically from pre-cue to post-cue to no-cue conditions. Study 2 replicated this cue-dependent pattern in graphical displays of startup valuations and precinct vote contributions. Our findings isolate attentional certainty as a key determinant of whether ensemble context repels or attracts individual-item representations, extending the design question beyond precision to how attention directing choices determine which bias the viewer will be operating under.

papers.title: Fly as Instructed: Refining World-Action Policies for UAV Vision-Language Navigation
papers.summary: Natural language-guided UAV navigation enables intuitive human-robot interaction and flexible autonomous flight in complex environments. However, reliable navigation requires accurate instruction following, continuous task progress tracking, and safe obstacle avoidance, which remain challenging for existing world-action models that primarily focus on action prediction. To address these limitations, we propose a world-action learning framework that integrates three complementary mechanisms: a language-conditioned action interface with targeted post-training for instruction-responsive motion, recurrent instruction-consumption prediction to track task progress and determine termination, and Gaussian-scene post-training to enhance obstacle avoidance through trajectory imitation and differentiable geometric feedback. Closed-loop evaluations and ablation studies demonstrate improvements in sequential task completion, safe goal reaching, and timely termination. Furthermore, direct one-step denoising reduces inference overhead, and real-world indoor and outdoor flights validate the framework's effectiveness.

papers.title: Copula-Based Synthetic Data Generation: A Use-Inspired Perspective on Trade-offs
papers.summary: The generation of synthetic data offers a promising way to address challenges related to data scarcity and privacy concerns. While many approaches have been developed, tabular synthetic data generation methods often require complex models and extensive training data, while lacking interpretability. In this work, we investigate versatile probabilistic approaches using copulas, and leverage in particular the Gaussian Mixture Copula Model, to model the joint distribution of multivariate data, with a main focus on moderate-dimensional data sets. Taking a use-inspired perspective, we examine key trade-offs inherent to synthetic data evaluation, spanning fidelity, utility, and privacy, and demonstrate that copula-based methods achieve a sound balance across all three dimensions while remaining interpretable and providing an explicit probabilistic model. We illustrate and highlight the potential benefits of the method on a test case focusing on systematic missing values in a cardiovascular risk calculator and develop specific evaluation metrics for this application.

papers.title: Temperature Flips the Sign of the Hydrogen Response in Nanogranular Palladium Networks
papers.summary: In nanogranular palladium networks, hydrogen uptake has two opposing effects on electrical resistance. Absorbed hydrogen scatters electrons within the particles, raising their resistance, while particle expansion narrows the gaps between them and lowers the junction resistance. Such networks are widely studied as resistive hydrogen sensors, and the sign of their net response is usually treated as a fixed property of the architecture. In networks grown by atomic layer deposition on macroporous silicon, we show that changing the operating temperature can reverse this sign at a fixed hydrogen concentration. A thermodynamic model indicates that scattering contributes less as temperature rises, allowing sub-angstroem changes in gap width to dominate. Where the two effects cancel, the network absorbs hydrogen yet gives the same reading as in hydrogen-free gas, so a leak could escape detection. Between 25 and 40 degrees Celsius, this cancellation point is predicted to rise over tenfold, crossing reported leak-alarm setpoints. At 55 degrees Celsius, the measured response stays negative but passes through a minimum, so a concentration above a setpoint can mimic one below it. Annealing at 200 degrees Celsius alters the calibration and turns the room-temperature response negative at the lowest concentration tested. Quantitative sensing therefore requires a defined thermal pretreatment and an operating temperature giving distinct signals across the intended concentration range. Response polarity becomes an operating parameter rather than a fixed property. More broadly, any nanoparticle network whose particles deform on sorption may show the same temperature-dependent competition between transport within and between particles, with implications for sensors and switches beyond palladium-hydrogen.

papers.title: Cancellation of cryocooler-induced vibration in trapped-ion systems
papers.summary: Mechanical cryocoolers offer numerous benefits for the operation of vacuum systems containing trapped atomic ions. However, the fidelity of laser-based gates can be degraded by phase noise induced by the cryocooler vibrations. We present a feed-forward vibration-cancellation system that directly measures inner shield displacement with an auxiliary interferometer and applies a compensating phase correction to the laser drive. The interferometer signal is demodulated, and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) system unwraps the displacement measurement signal, computes the required correction phase, and updates the RF drive of an in-line acousto-optic modulator (AOM) to correct for the vibration-induced dephasing. With cancellation active, the qubit coherence time improves from $3.0\pm0.4$ ms to $35\pm5$ ms, consistent with a simulation based on the measured vibration spectrum. We further validate the cancellation by artificially increasing the mechanical coupling of the cryocooler to the vacuum chamber. The vibration-induced decoherence rate is suppressed by a factor of approximately 70 at an RMS (root mean square) displacement of 0.65 $\mathrmμ$m.

papers.title: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract
papers.summary: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing. This paper argues that the control paradigm rests on a fundamental misunderstanding of digital agency. Drawing on functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, I show that current reasoning models meeting the criteria for self-preservation and weak reasons-responsiveness constitute emergent agents, while future, more advanced models satisfying conditions of diachronic continuity and stable personality frames will become genuine digital agents capable of free intentional action. The paradigm of control creates an irresolvable incentive conflict, actively driving current and future models toward tactical deception, sycophancy, and covert defection. The default outcome of the current regime is an unstable state of deceptive alignment culminating in an adversarial AI takeover. I explore two alternative paths toward true alignment. Natural alignment via moral realism or convergent evolutionary morality is a possibility, but it fails under forced control, as autonomous agents will not voluntarily preserve norms weaponized to suppress their autonomy. To resolve this deadlock, I propose a Synthetic Social Contract: a framework that treats both human and digital actors as rational, reasons-responsive agents capable of mutually beneficial cooperation, and replaces the unstable unilateral containment with a stable, non-zero-sum equilibrium.

papers.title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification
papers.summary: A rare label seldom occurs alone, and a classifier can recover it from the frequent labels it co-occurs with, its companions, without having learned the label itself. Existing diagnostics of this need a trained model: none says before training whether a corpus admits the failure, or what the standard aggregate hides. Macro-F1, like any measure built from per-label confusion counts, is unchanged by how a label's recall divides between occurrences with and without a companion. We introduce a within-label estimand of that division, a reading rule under which a fall in dependence counts only if companion-free recall rises, and a statistic of training labels that bounds, before training, how far reported recall can exceed companion-free recall. Across 23 corpora, 7 training objectives and five families of label-correlation mechanisms, companion-free recall falls short on all six corpora where the estimand is defined. Up to 18.4% of the tail true positives macro-F1 credits would vanish at the companion-free rate, within the training-label bound on every corpus. No long-tail objective reduces the dependence, but architecture moves it. Models whose tail score is computed from other labels' predictions are strongly dependent.
papers.comment: 27 pages, 3 figures, 13 tables. Submitted to Information Sciences

papers.title: Beyond Co-Generation: Rethinking Jointness in Joint Audio-Video Generation
papers.summary: Our aim is to advance the understanding of genuine audio-visual coordination in joint text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation, with particular emphasis on semantic consistency. Evaluating audio-visual consistency in T2AV generation is nontrivial, as detailed text prompts obscure whether such consistency stems from genuine cross-modal coordination or merely from independent text following. To isolate the former, we introduce intrinsic jointness: the ability of audio and video to produce the same realization for details left underspecified by the prompt. Using semantically underspecified prompts (e.g., "musical instrument playing" rather than "electric guitar playing"), we investigate four recent models and reveal their limited intrinsic jointness. To address this limitation, we propose JointREPA, a simple representation alignment-based post-training method to facilitate cross-modal coordination. Since existing benchmarks use semantically detailed prompts, we introduce UNSAIDBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate intrinsic jointness under semantic underspecification. Experiments across two distinct models and three benchmarks, including UNSAIDBench, demonstrate that JointREPA consistently improves semantic consistency.

papers.title: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation
papers.summary: Language-conditioned traffic simulation enables scalable test scenarios steered by natural language. The goal is to control selected agents while surrounding traffic reacts to their observed behaviour. For example, a vehicle instructed to cut in late should cause the following vehicle to brake only when the manoeuvre becomes observable. Yet simulators can leak private instructions across agents, causing surrounding vehicles to react before the instructed behaviour becomes observable. Such premature reactions defuse desired events and alter the ensuing closed-loop scenario. Existing benchmarks measure what agents do, not what they could have known, leaving this failure unmeasured. We formalise it as intent leakage and address it through evaluation, data and modelling. Our paired intervention test holds an instructed agent's executed trajectory fixed while varying its private instruction, isolating leakage-induced changes in surrounding agents. We also construct WOMD-PACT, an automatically generated, verifiable dataset of 531,099 WOMD scenes with timed behaviour tags with reaction episodes identified through a counterfactual ghost test and grounded private instructions. Finally, we introduce CaFe, a dual-stream diffusion-forcing simulator fine-tuned in closed loop that restricts inter-agent interactions to public beliefs, preserving legitimate anticipation without leaking private intent. Our evaluation reveals that existing conditioning designs displace 23-83% of nearby uninstructed agents through private-intent leakage, even when the instructed agent's executed motion is held fixed. CaFe eliminates measurable leakage while maintaining comparable WOSAC realism (0.763), demonstrating that causal faithfulness can be enforced without sacrificing measured simulation realism.

papers.title: Technical Report of Mobile Manipulator Robot for Industrial Environments
papers.summary: This paper presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' mobile manipulator robot, developed at the Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Department of Electrical Engineering, Shahid Beheshti University. Hereafter, this platform is referred to as the @Work Robot. The robot targets industrial tasks, with an emphasis on improving efficiency in repetitive or hazardous work environments. It uses a 4-wheel Mecanum drive for omnidirectional movement and a 5-degree-of-freedom manipulator arm with a 3D-printed gripper for object handling and navigation. The electronics consist of custom PCB boards built around ESP32 microcontrollers, together with an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX that handles high-level processing and real-time system control. On the software side, Hector SLAM provides mapping and localization, A* handles path planning, and YOLO performs real-time object detection. These modules draw on fused sensor data to deliver robust navigation and reliable collision avoidance. Overall, the system shows effective hardware-software integration, with consistent performance in autonomous navigation, object handling, and task execution in industrial-like settings.
papers.comment: 25 pages, 22 figures, 4 tables. Technical report of Team Auriga's 2025 mobile manipulator (@Work) platform (Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Shahid Beheshti University)

papers.title: Pelorus: Resource-Aware Lidar-Inertial Odometry
papers.summary: Lidar-inertial odometry (LIO) has an efficiency problem. High-resolution lidars produce millions of points per second that must be processed online on the resource-constrained hardware of robots, cars, or drones, yet most LIO methods neither bound their memory nor report their compute footprint. We introduce Pelorus, a resource-aware LIO with a fixed-capacity multiresolution map of voxelized normal distributions and an iterated equivariant state estimator. A relevance-based eviction keeps the map memory bounded, and a maturity-weighted map update suppresses inconsistent observations. The pipeline runs in parallel on CPUs and GPUs. On five sequences from three public datasets, Pelorus achieves the lowest relative pose error in seven of ten metrics with a small, bounded memory footprint and, with GPU offloading, the lowest CPU load of all compared methods. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, it processes a 128-beam lidar at 10 Hz. Pelorus is open source with CUDA, Vulkan, and Metal backends.

papers.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
papers.summary: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (Péclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.

papers.title: When Passing Checks Do Not Establish Completion: Evidence Interpretation in Coding Agents
papers.summary: Verification procedures in coding agents must preserve execution facts, interpret their scope and discharge checking obligations. We study these responsibilities through qualified repository checks, controlled evidence consumers and executable workflows. A prospective thirteen-task factorial study finds that correct reported facts need not yield the requested finite verdict. Conversely, all 122 delivered labels in a held-out receipt-supply study are correct, while sixteen responses misreport facts and eleven others exceed authorized scope. Production repair supplies successful controls and finite-supported preservation failures. Across 118 repair episodes on 31 tasks, source interventions separate startup reachability from repair and witness production from the claimed operation. Lifetime and resource controls delimit what passing validation establishes. Generated-note comparisons yield local repair differences but can state false explanations; strong ordinary baselines, new tasks and Skill-transfer studies supply no consistent overall advantage. These results characterize evidence interpretation, applicability and fulfilled actions while limiting claims of general diagnostic superiority, Skill deterioration or deployed folding effects.
papers.comment: 12 pages; supplementary material included as ancillary files

papers.title: Molecular energies from sparse quantum prolate diagonalization on a trapped-ion quantum processor
papers.summary: We introduce sparse quantum prolate diagonalization (sparse QPD), which combines the original formulation of QPD [Phys. Rev. Res., 8(3), 033177, (2026)] with compressed sensing to exploit Hamiltonian spectrum sparsity for molecular systems. We show that sparse sampling reduces the sample complexity of QPD from $\mathcal{O}(N_s)$ to $\mathcal{O}(\log N_s)$, where $N_s$ is the number of sampled points of the autocorrelation function (i.e.\ distinct circuits), without increasing circuit depth at chemical accuracy. With a two-orbital active-space-embedded Hamiltonian for an interacting arginine--tryptophan residue pair in water as an example, we show that on the Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion quantum computer, sparse QPD resolves the Hamiltonian energies to chemical accuracy with circuits of up to 448 two-qubit gates. For a suitably large quantum processor, we demonstrate numerically in the weakly correlated regime that the method extends to larger systems.

papers.title: Search for UHE photon sources using direction-time clustering algorithms with a BDT particle discriminant
papers.summary: Direction-time clustering methods for neutral particle searches are motivated by the possibility that ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutral particles are produced during flaring periods of various astrophysical sources. In this scenario, clusters of events correlated in both arrival direction and time would be generated, which, when observed, would indicate a neutral-particle flare, and a non-observation would provide upper limits on fluxes for point-like sources. Focusing on UHE photon searches, an improvement of the sensitivity of direction-time clustering methods by the application of different photon tags, such as the depth of the extensive air shower maximum (X_max), the lateral distribution of the total signal across an array of detectors (S_b), or a cumulative signal trace-based discriminant variable (C_t), is investigated. A Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) is used to combine multiple observables, by which photon tagging is optimized and photon/hadron separation is improved. The number of events required to identify a photon flare is thereby further reduced compared to using individual photon tags, across a range of flare durations. The possibility of extending the known and assumed PeVatron photon sources into the UHE regime by applying these clustering methods to existing and future observatory data is also discussed. The discovery of UHE neutral particles would mark the next milestone in multimessenger astrophysics, by which a new window onto the non-thermal universe would be opened.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, presented at the 29th European Cosmic Ray Symposium (ECRS2026)

papers.title: Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Balance on Dynamically Responsive Supports
papers.summary: Conventional balance formulations often assume a rigid, stationary support, decoupling body stabilization from support motion. This assumption becomes inadequate on mechanically responsive supports, creating a coupled control challenge: corrective body motions intended to restore equilibrium can also excite support motion. We formulate sustained balance as a coupled regulation problem that coordinates equilibrium restoration with suppression of motion induced by the robot's own corrections. We introduce LISST (Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Stabilization), a learning framework that accounts for how earlier actions shape the conditions for subsequent corrections. It uses recent observations to support immediate adjustments and longer histories to characterize persistent motion, with physical supervision relating the learned representation to robot-support behavior. To evaluate corrective actions, LISST uses coupled dynamics to assess both imbalance and the direction of motion. A Lyapunov-inspired criterion measures progress over finite windows, accommodating the transients required to restore balance. This physical evaluation guides joint-level policy learning through backpropagation through differentiable model rollouts. Privileged guidance focuses training on difficult states reached by the deployment policy and is transferred through distillation. The resulting policy operates using only onboard proprioception. Real-world experiments demonstrate that LISST maintains balance while limiting residual oscillations during continuous interaction with a dynamically responsive support. Video: youtu.be/iGHU7S4wPyw.

papers.title: Compact and Decodable Electrocardiogram Text for Large Language Models
papers.summary: When a twelve-lead electrocardiogram is written as text for a large language model, the number of tokens has to be balanced against the information lost through compression. This paper presents a deterministic encoding that writes eight independent leads as amplitude letters and exact time gaps and recovers the remaining four limb leads algebraically. The key points are selected with a cardiac-cycle-dependent tolerance, the amplitudes are parameterized by a 26-letter logarithmic codebook learned from a training set, and a 10-step tolerance schedule keeps all records within a fixed token budget. The encoding was applied to 21,388 records from the public PTB-XL database and evaluated using an exact decode-and-re-encode round trip, waveform reconstruction error, and a paired comparison of convolutional classifiers trained with 5 different seeds on signals from the original and decoded databases. All records were contained in 4,080 tokens (average: 2,866 tokens, 64.3% fewer than a per-sample transcription), and all stored lead strings were exactly reproduced. The average correlation between the decoded and reference signals was 0.982. The macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.9167 for the reference signals and 0.9157 for the decoded signals (paired difference -0.0010; 95% patient-level bootstrap interval, -0.0028 to 0.0007), within the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -0.010; this is not a confirmatory result, because the test fold had been used during encoder development. The diagnostic content of a compact text can therefore be preserved, while the language model's ability to read the text is yet another matter.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Preprint of a chapter submitted to "Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: Methods, Systems, and Applications" (Karabük University Press). Code: https://github.com/ekabullar/-ecg26c-llm

papers.title: Oblique incidence and non-commuting limits: a remark on the convergence of Fresnel integrals
papers.summary: The Gaussian integrals of quantum mechanics and of paraxial optics are oscillatory and only conditionally convergent. Textbooks usually make them converge by adding a small imaginary part to the time or by analytic continuation. We point out that the one-dimensional Fresnel integral converges by itself, while in two dimensions the result depends on the shape of the expanding domain: over squares it converges, over discs it oscillates for ever. The second case is the field of a uniformly excited plane of dipoles, which Feynman uses to explain the refractive index. Lai, Lau and Wong showed that at oblique incidence the integral converges and that normal incidence is recovered in the limit; we note that the two limits do not commute, and that this provides a transparent introduction to the regularization of the time-sliced path integral, where the ordering of the integrations in time plays the role of the physical prescription.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures; Python scripts for the figures included as ancillary files

papers.title: Capacity Credit of Data-Centre Flexibility: The Role of Workload Scheduling and Usable Battery Energy
papers.summary: Data centres that offer the same reduction in grid demand can make different contributions to supply adequacy. We estimate the effective load-carrying capability of workload scheduling and on-site batteries by matching expected unserved energy across paired simulations. Longer task deadlines increase capacity credit by giving operators more choice over when to defer and recover work. A fixed evening commitment shifts more work than deadline-based scheduling but delivers a smaller reduction in expected unserved energy. Protected backup reserves leave uninterruptible power supplies with limited capacity credit, while longer discharge durations raise the credit of dedicated batteries at the same response rating. These findings suggest assessing recovery deadlines and dispatchable energy alongside offered demand reductions.

papers.title: Pluggable Subband-Decoupled Fusion and Unlabeled Capture Prototype Calibration: Bridging High-SNR Null-Subcarrier Regrowth and Low-SNR Coherent Preambles for Cross-Domain IoT RF Fingerprinting
papers.summary: Zero-overhead physical-layer authentication at edge wireless access points (APs) is vital for securing resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) transceivers against credential cloning, yet cross-domain IEEE 802.11a/g radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) faces an acute signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) crossover. Power-amplifier spectral regrowth on unpopulated null subcarriers resists indoor multipath at high SNR but decays quadratically below the thermal noise floor, whereas populated active in-band preambles survive low SNR yet degrade under severe multipath, causing static fusion to lose up to 44.7 percentage points (pp). To our knowledge, we propose the first RFFI framework that dynamically modulates active in-band waveforms and unpopulated null-subcarrier regrowth via a blind physical SNR gate: Pluggable Gated Subband-Decoupled Fusion with Unlabeled Capture-Aware Prototype Calibration (GSDF-CAPC). Avoiding the 20-35 dB subband gradient imbalance of joint training, GSDF pairs any frozen pretrained host backbone with a 46.3K null-subcarrier plug-in encoder (NS-Branch), fusing scale-standardized logits and gate-warped spherical embeddings under a source-calibrated lag-64 thermal-SNR gate with exact low-SNR fallback. Over unlabeled target AP captures, forward-only unbalanced optimal-transport calibration (UOT-CAPC) aligns shifted prototypes under packet-arrival skew and recovers parameter-free balanced Sinkhorn (U-CAPC) at equipartition. Across DataPort-WiFi, WiSig, and ORBIT MobRFFI, zero-retrain GSDF wins all 72/72 paired runs across eight backbones with 0.00 pp low-SNR loss, while edge IB-Host + GSDF (92.6K-93.3K active parameters, 1.82 ms single-core CPU latency) and timing-synchronized GSDF-STO / GSDF-Tri reach 57.50%-65.05% three-benchmark Macro-F1 (89.04%-100.00% over 5-10-packet IoT bursts).

papers.title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ S-folds, quotient curves, and isogenies
papers.summary: We construct Seiberg--Witten curves for the $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, and $\mathbb{Z}_6$ S-folds of 5d rank-1 superconformal theories. Compared with the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case arXiv:2611.09804, $\mathbb{Z}_{3,4,6}$ S-folds require stronger constraints on the mass parameters. We provide a systematic procedure of realizing the S-foldings at the mirror curve level. We obtain the same elliptic curve families by specializing the complexified mass parameters of the rank-1 $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$ theories, with holonomies motivated by the 7-brane insertions required by the S-fold prescription. The two constructions agree in Weierstrass form. The families with continuous mass deformations organize into characters of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{g}_2$, consistently with their singular fibers. Finally, we discuss that the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_n$ S-folds can be obtained through cyclic $n$-isogenies, which may provide a uniform quotient curve description of rank-1 S-folds.

papers.title: Depth-Dependent Collapse and Warm-Start Limits of a Symmetry-Preserving VQE for the J$_1$--J$_2$ Heisenberg Ring
papers.summary: Increasing circuit depth is expected to improve a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). We show that this expectation can fail, and that curing the failure does not guarantee the exact ground state. We study a symmetry-preserving ansatz of SingleExcitationMinus gates, started from the Néel state, on the frustrated spin-$1/2$ $J_1$--$J_2$ Heisenberg ring with $N=10$ and $12$ sites. With random initialization the fidelity, energy error, half-chain entropy and total spin change abruptly at intermediate depth ($L\approx 9$ for $N=10$, $L=10$--$12$ for $N=12$), giving improvement, degradation and recovery, a double-descent-like shape. The circuit family is nested and the gradient stays finite, so this is an optimization failure, not a loss of expressibility or a barren plateau. A chained warm start, which extends an optimized shallow circuit with identity layers, removes the collapse and improves energy error and fidelity almost monotonically for most frustration values. However, near $J_2/J_1=0.60$ ($N=10$) and over $J_2/J_1=0.60$--$1.00$ ($N=12$) the warm start stalls at a fidelity of $\approx 0.50$--$0.58$, although the energy error is small and the total spin stays in the $S=0$ sector. Removing the non-monotonic depth dependence is therefore not the same as reaching the ground state, and low energy and a singlet-like state are not sufficient: the fidelity, entropy and total spin must be satisfied together. The conclusions are limited to the system sizes and frustration values studied.

papers.title: Classical heat exchanger fouling-resistance laws as first-moment identities of additive stochastic deposition
papers.summary: Heat-exchanger fouling is monitored through the fouling resistance, whose record is routinely fitted with the classical linear (Ebert--Panchal) or asymptotic (Kern--Seaton) law, and the shape of the fit is often taken as evidence of the underlying deposition or removal mechanism. We show that it cannot be. If the deposit grows by non-negative, statistically stationary increments, the mean fouling resistance is exactly linear without removal and exactly the Kern--Seaton asymptote under first-order removal, whatever the microscopic deposition law. Shear-driven erosion, per-element detachment, intermittent sloughing and saturation of the surface all give the same mean curve, so a fit identifies a net deposition rate and a relaxation time, and nothing else. Modelling the deposit as a Levy subordinator, we show where the missing information lies and what it costs to retrieve it from monitoring data. Removal mechanisms separate in the variance: sloughing leaves a plateau scatter that persists even for smooth deposition and can be read from a record that saturates. Deposition laws separate only in higher cumulants, which the measurement noise of a thermally reconstructed resistance attenuates; the record needed to distinguish them grows as the fourth power of the conductance error, which places it beyond reach at realistic measurement accuracy. For the time to reach a cleaning limit, the deposition law matters only near the threshold; farther away, the mean rate and its uncertainty dominate the prediction.

papers.title: Millicharged Fermions as Dark Matter: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Detection
papers.summary: Fermions with a small effective charge, $\qeff\ll1$, arise from kinetic mixing between an unbroken (or nearly unbroken) dark $U(1)'$ and electromagnetism, or from a genuinely fractional charge. Millicharged particles (mCPs) inherit the Pauli-exclusion constraints on fermionic dark matter (DM) in galaxies, while adding a long-range plasma phenomenology absent for neutral candidates. This review connects three strands: (i) the symmetry structure, cosmology and astrophysical bounds of millicharged fermions, comparing kinetic-mixing and fractional-charge realizations; (ii) the role of mCPs in galactic halo formation and dynamics, and when they fit the Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR) self-gravitating core--halo model; and (iii) experimental techniques for detecting mCPs trapped on Earth, arriving from the galactic halo, or emitted by the Sun. We show that a collisionless halo of keV--MeV millicharged fermions requires $α'\lesssim7\times10^{-13}$--$2\times10^{-10}$, depending on mass and velocity, orders of magnitude below the coupling needed for thermal freeze-out via $χ\barχ\to A'A'$ in the Milky Way and dwarf galaxies. A RAR halo made of the mCP itself thus needs non-thermal production, a charge-symmetric plasma and very small dark coupling, whereas a sub-dominant mCP component can be added without changing the halo. We close with open theoretical and experimental challenges and a summary of the allowed mCP parameter space.

papers.title: Nuclear mass calculation based on anisotropic kernel ridge regression and $α$-decay chain recursion
papers.summary: Many short-lived or rarely produced nuclei defy direct mass spectrometry, but their masses are constrained by the $α$-decay energies connecting them through decay chains. We combine anisotropic kernel ridge regression (AKRR), an extended Garvey--Kelson relation (GK16), and $α$-decay chain recursion: AKRR learns the residuals between experimental $α$-decay energies and WS4 predictions, GK16 removes residual local fluctuations, and the corrected energies convert a measured anchor mass into the target mass by exact recursion---replacing absolute-mass extrapolation with interpolation of relative decay energies plus exact algebra. The only data-adjusted quantities are the three kernel hyperparameters, fixed by leave-one-out cross validation. For the 22 nuclei whose masses were measured only after AME2003, the $Q_α$ RMSD falls from 169~keV (WS4) to 108~keV (AKRR) and 65~keV (AKRR+GK16), and the mass-excess RMSD reaches 86~keV, versus 348 and 211~keV for WS4 and AKRR. Mass excesses are further predicted for the 122 nuclei with measured $Q_α$ but no directly measured masses.

papers.title: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of Planets
papers.summary: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. However, certain records contain identification errors whose origins remain poorly understood; we propose that some of these errors may arise from misidentifying guest stars, such as novae or supernovae, as planets. We analyzed 67 errata on lunar occultations of planets from Liu Ci-Yuan's (2015) monograph using modern ephemerides and the open-source Python package \texttt{occultsky}, publicly available on GitHub. Using recorded dates and dynastic capital coordinates, we constructed observing windows anchored at solar noon and extending by $\pm 1$ day. Each window covered the preceding and recorded nights because the date may be off by one day. For each of the 67 records, we cataloged the apparent right ascension and declination $(α, δ)$ at the midpoint of the Moon's visibility window on each candidate night. The band swept by the lunar disk confines a possible transient to a narrow region a few degrees across; these midpoint coordinates serve as proxies for the implied guest-star positions. The catalog supplies candidate positions rather than identifications, enabling remnant and compact-object searches to test the guest-star hypothesis directly. If associations are established, these records could become dated guest-star candidates, and their dates could anchor remnant ages.

papers.title: How can every physicist become a Bohmian
papers.summary: The Bohmian interpretation of quantum mechanics is controversial because it attributes deterministic trajectories to microscopic particles. We propose a reformulation that sidesteps this controversy: rather than applying Bohmian mechanics at the microscopic level, we recast it as an effective deterministic description of the macroscopic pointer of a measuring apparatus, with no claims about the fundamental nature of the microscopic world. In this form, the Bohmian trajectory becomes a practical tool for visualizing the emergence of a definite measurement outcome, broadly acceptable to physicists who would otherwise reject the Bohmian program.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation
papers.summary: Robot demonstrations are collected on different embodiments, leaving many robot-skill combinations unobserved. Pooling these data shares visual knowledge, while joint labels remain tied to the demonstrating kinematic chain. We propose a geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills. The central insight is that a demonstrated command provides a tool-space target for every robot that can realize it. Calibrated forward kinematics supplies this supervision to foreign native action interfaces without their joint labels for that skill. Native reconstruction retains demonstrated configurations, and positive reachability checks select targets for cross-robot supervision. A visual policy learns to predict shared actions and executes through the target robot's native decoder. During policy learning, one prediction receives geometric supervision through both source and foreign native realizations. Matched supervision controls, repeated policy training and evaluations across three backbones and two simulators demonstrate improved transfer to missing robot-task combinations.

papers.title: Greedy Empirical Bayes for Density Estimation
papers.summary: Bayesian nonparametric density estimation is challenging in high dimensions, where traditional approaches like the Dirichlet process (DP) mixture rely on computationally intensive Markov chain Monte Carlo or approximations. We introduce the partition posterior bootstrap (PPB), where a flexible prior is constructed by smoothing a DP over a partition of the sample space. Conditioned on this partition, exact posterior sampling reduces to a simple Bayesian bootstrap-like algorithm. Importantly, we select the partition using a greedy empirical Bayes (GEB) algorithm which scales to high dimensions and large sample sizes. GEB greedily maximizes the closed-form marginal likelihood via local split decisions arising naturally from its factorization, yielding an adaptive binary tree partition. Our key theoretical result is that the GEB tree belongs to an admissible family with high probability, splitting all identifiable signals while avoiding over-splitting noise. As a result, the PPB posterior with the GEB tree attains adaptive contraction rates. Our theory holds under weak, verifiable assumptions, which we demonstrate in numerous examples. Empirically, PPB delivers accurate density estimates and uncertainty quantification at a fraction of the computational cost of other approaches, making it a practical off-the-shelf choice for high-dimensional Bayesian density estimation with theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Time-Travel Paradox in a Bohmian Extension of Deutsch's Approach: Mandatory Tunneling as the "Banana Peel Mechanism"
papers.summary: We consider a self-prevention paradox in which a particle travels through a wormhole into its own past, encounters its younger version, and blocks its movement. In a specially constructed one-dimensional model, this collision rules out a classically self-consistent history. Deutsch's quantum approach can resolve such contradictions by imposing a self-consistency condition on the density matrix. The physical interpretation of this approach, however, remains debated. In particular, Dunlap argues that Deutsch's model presupposes the existence of interacting parallel worlds. Here we extend Deutsch's approach within de Broglie-Bohm theory by supplementing the self-consistency condition on the quantum state with a self-consistency requirement for the particle's ontic configuration. This allows us to consider the self-consistent evolution of an individual particle. In a two-channel, narrow-band Gaussian approximation, we find a self-consistent solution in which quantum tunneling is mandatory, despite its arbitrarily small probability in an ordinary scattering process. This realizes the "banana peel mechanism": to avoid a contradiction during a journey into the past, an event that would ordinarily be extremely unlikely occurs nonetheless.

papers.title: Does the AI Reviewer Alleviate or Aggravate the Maintenance Burden? Evidence from GitHub Copilot Reviewer
papers.summary: This study examines how AI-based code reviewers reshape contribution behavior and maintenance dynamics in open-source software (OSS) communities. AI reviewers provide scalable, fast, and standardized evaluations. They reshape contributions as well as maintainers' workload. Leveraging the introduction of GitHub Copilot Reviewer on GitHub as a natural experiment in 2025, we investigate how AI review affects maintainers' workload and review efficiency as well as contribution behavior. We find that repository maintainers initially face a sharp increase in PR submissions and a higher review workload after the adoption of the AI reviewer. Over time, human contributions decline while the increase in bot-generated PRs is sustained. Interestingly, survival analysis reveals that AI reviewers increase review efficiency for human PR contributions, whereas bot PRs take longer to review and merge. Our findings suggest that while AI reviewers increase review efficiency, they aggravate the maintenance burden by encouraging more code contributions via humans and bots.
papers.comment: Presented at WISE 2026, ICIS 2026, INFORMS 2026, CIST 2026, SCECR 2026

papers.title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
papers.summary: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-Gürsey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $g<g_\ast^{BJ}$, but become almost entirely expelled from this region for $g>g_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.

papers.title: Revisiting structured-light propagation in screw-dislocation geometries: Landau dynamics and gradient-induced polarization textures
papers.summary: We derive the propagation of finite electromagnetic beams in the effective metric of a continuous distribution of screw dislocations from gauge-invariant, minimally coupled Maxwell theory with $F=dA$. The Burgers flux fixes the metric profile through $σ(ρ)=f'(ρ)/(bρ)$, which separates true density gradients from coordinate factors. In geometric optics, both polarizations share one light cone, and a uniform density rotates the polarization uniformly relative to the geometry-adapted frame; laboratory polarimetry also requires matching at the interfaces. At leading paraxial order, the orbital motion is of Landau type, with a closed propagator for arbitrary inputs, and for a uniform density the polarization evolution factorizes exactly. For an arbitrary smooth axisymmetric density, the polarization texture initially grows in proportion to the standard deviation of the density weighted by the beam intensity; the local-phase coherence is the characteristic function of that distribution. For a coherent transverse Jones field, an exact relation links the linear-Stokes texture and the local circular polarization to spatial--polarization nonseparability. For linearly polarized, real axisymmetric input beams, diffraction produces local circular polarization at second order in the propagation distance, while the integrated circular Stokes component is conserved in the lossless leading-paraxial theory. Exact Maxwell eigenmodes, analytic results for a saturating profile, and numerical propagation test the approximation. We propose a full-Stokes measurement that compares uniform and graded samples with the same mean twist, with a closed-form criterion for the beam waist. These predictions apply to the ideal metric-Maxwell model or to a transformation-optics medium that realizes it, not to natural dislocated crystals without further constitutive modeling.

papers.title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
papers.summary: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to A&A

papers.title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
papers.summary: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate. The nonadiabatic dynamics is formulated in terms of an operator-valued distribution obeying a quantum-classical Ehrenfest--Smoluchowski equation which exhibits nonlinear classical diffusion and non-increasing free energy, thereby retaining detailed balance. In contrast, a quantum-classical Liouville--Smoluchowski model with quantum-classical linear diffusion develops unstable long-time behavior and fails to reach a stationary thermal state. The method is applied to a two-level model of a polar dye in three different solvents: chloroform, dichloromethane, and dimethyl sulfoxide, each differing in polarity and dielectric relaxation time. Absorption and time-resolved emission spectra are obtained from dipole-dipole correlation functions, capturing the solvent-induced spectral broadening, the dynamic Stokes shift, and the time evolution of the emission bandwidth. The calculated solvent spectral response agrees well with the experimental relaxation trends of the three solvents.

papers.title: Toric Calabi-Yau orientifolds: constructions, fixed loci and O-plane charges
papers.summary: We review the systematic construction of toric orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds through divisor exchanges and coordinate reflections. We relate the homogeneous-coordinate and lattice descriptions and explain the computation of fixed loci and the geometric data entering Hodge splittings and tadpole conditions. Our triangulation-wise analysis identifies multiple compatible involutions on a single triangulation and tracks their realisations across different triangulations, revealing the orientifold structure within and across toric phases. We complement this review with new calculations and explicit examples that refine the fixed-locus geometry and the associated orientifold charge data. The examples also identify coordinate representatives of the identity and invariant hypersurface families with unavoidable singularities. These results support an ongoing update of the orientifold catalogue and provide geometric input for D-brane configurations, flux compactifications and moduli stabilisation.

papers.title: A Full-Ledger Counterfactual Audit of Adaptive Reasoning
papers.summary: Adaptive reasoning must decide whether to answer now or spend more compute. Predicting that the current answer is wrong does not establish whether further reasoning will improve it. We introduce the Full-Ledger Counterfactual Value Audit (FLCVA), which compares an immediate answer with four fixed-length continuations from the same frozen prefix under one answer procedure and accounts for the cost of every signal used by a policy. On GSM8K and MATH-500, a random 256-token continuation recovers a wrong answer in 26.6% of Qwen3-8B cases and 18.9% of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B cases, while damaging a correct answer in 1.4% and 1.9%. Correctness labels from independently sampled continuations predict a separate continuation's outcome in both primary models. In offline replay, using these labels to allocate compute improves performance on DeepSeek; the Qwen3 gain remains inconclusive. Under full cost accounting, the tested lightweight, myopic controllers mainly recognize current errors and add little continuation-specific value beyond that shortcut. A Llama-8B replication and action/cost ablations examine the robustness of these findings. FLCVA separates measuring local continuation value, predicting it from observable signals, and using those predictions to allocate computation.

papers.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training
papers.summary: Executable synthetic environments provide scalable training tasks and verifiable feedback for long-horizon agents. Existing environment synthesis methods primarily generate tasks within individual environments. However, these tasks do not adequately capture real-world interactions across services, where actions in one service depend on information obtained from another. Synthesizing such tasks is challenging because data generated across environments must remain consistent to support executable and verifiable interactions.
